description: An external busy input that clears before a received EOT end time does not delay the idle: csma.vdcd_end starts when the input clears, the idle at the EOT end time is VDCD-determined and produced by the end of that transmission, and LBT rule 1 gives a zero wait.
note: Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for non-ARQ and gets S_BIND_ACCEPTED (A-0041, A-0047); its S_UNIDATA_REQUEST (priority 0 to SAP 5 at 0.0.1.3, U_PDU "hello", no confirmation) is data queued for transmission and produces no SIS output (A-0095, K-0096). The DTS keeps dts.ttd at the earliest TTD in its transmit queue (C-1050). channel_busy true at 1000 with nothing queued: no output (K-0065). The request at 2000 finds the channel busy, so the node waits in SENSE (K-0066). The bytes at 4000 are those of csma-two-node-zero-lbt: a single-segment NON-ARQ-DATA from 0.0.1.3 to this node (C_PDU ID 1, EOT 10, so end 9000) and one from 0.0.1.3 to the broadcast address (C_PDU ID 2, EOT 10), so two-node condition (a) holds over this transmission (K-0068, K-0072); the S_PDUs are for SAP 9, which no client has bound, so no output (A-0235). The burst ends at 6000 with the external input still busy, so csma.vdcd_end is not started yet (K-0111). The external input clears at 7000 with DCD false and the end time 9000 still ahead: csma.vdcd_end starts for 2000 ms. At 9000 the idle is VDCD-determined and the transmission's end produced it, so rule 1 gives zero: no LBT_WAIT_TIMER is started (zero-duration rule) and the node enters CONT_WAIT at once with the first draw of seed 0, uniform(16) = 15, so 45000 ms (K-0067, K-0079, K-0109). Compare csma-external-busy-outlasts-eot.
